findings.reason: The original standalone tiles contain no illustration. A commuting free-extension triangle materially clarifies the distinction between the set-indexed elementary-tensor family and its linear extension on the free module; it does not suggest that an arbitrary tensor is elementary or that the bases are finite. Under the expanded explanatory-diagram scope this is a warranted missing illustration, although the existing proof and formulas already render correctly.
findings.action: Appended a final Remarks section with a tikzcd triangle, explicit map definitions, the finite-support linear-extension formula, and empty-index/choice qualifications.

correction: Added only final Remarks (lines 64–77): I×J maps by iota to R^(I×J), by b to M tensor_R N, and Phi is the canonical module isomorphism with Phi composed with iota = b.

diagram_math_checks.result: I and J remain arbitrary basis index sets from the Statement. iota:I×J→R^(I×J) sends (i,j) to its standard vector u_(i,j); b:I×J→M tensor_R N sends (i,j) to e_i tensor f_j. Both are set maps. Phi:R^(I×J)→M tensor_R N is R-linear, given by L4 and the Statement. No injectivity of iota is asserted (including the zero-ring case).
diagram_math_checks.justification: Read current def-free-module-on-a-set-and-standard-basis and thm-universal-property-of-free-modules; local L3/L4 and proof 1.1.

diagram_math_checks.result: The only asserted triangle relation is Phi∘iota=b, checked at each (i,j) by Phi(u_(i,j))=e_i tensor f_j. The right downward map alone bears the isomorphism symbol.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Proof 2.1 constructs the isomorphism using direct-sum distribution and R tensor_R R≅R; proof 3.1 traces exactly these coordinate generators. Read both named local suppliers.

diagram_math_checks.result: The coefficient family c_ij lies in the direct sum R^(I×J), hence has finite support, so both displayed sums are finite. Linearity gives the formula; the figure contains no finite rectangular grid and makes no finite-rank assumption.
diagram_math_checks.justification: L3, the current free-module definition, and proof 3.1 give unique finite coordinate expressions.

diagram_math_checks.result: If I or J is empty, I×J is empty, R^(I×J)=0 and M tensor_R N=0; iota and b are the empty set maps and Phi is the unique zero-module isomorphism. The bases are supplied in the hypotheses; the illustration chooses no new basis or coordinates beyond them.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Statement and proof 3.2; free-module definition includes the empty basis; universal-property supplier explicitly handles the empty set without hidden choice.

diagram_math_checks.result: All original proof bytes are retained; the added triangle cites the proved coordinate calculation and is not used as a proof premise.
